subject: HIPAA onboarding: HSM escrow vs metered KMS — decision and finance ask

Subject: HIPAA onboarding: HSM escrow vs metered KMS — decision and finance ask

Hi all,

Quick thread to get alignment on the pricing packaging for Carlisle's HIPAA pilot. Procurement surfaced two competing asks: an "escrow/onboarding amortization" for HSM hardware & provisioning, or a pure metered KMS model (no upfront HSM charge) with a higher per-1k-key rate. They expect a procurement decision in ~2 weeks.

I've sketched three commercial paths in the attached Residency_Pricing_Options.xlsx:
- Option A: Upfront HSM escrow (one-time onboarding fee amortized over 12 months) + discounted per-token inference pricing.
- Option B: No upfront escrow, metered KMS (per-1k key ops) and higher recurring premium for HSM-backed operations.
- Option C: Hybrid — small onboarding deposit (refundable against 12-month commit) + blended metered KMS with step-down after commit thresholds.

Ask: Ben/Stephanie, I need recommendation on which path we should present formally. Key constraints: Carlisle wants a predictable FY29 spend, but legal wants HSM evidence and a mechanism to ensure keys remain segregated. Procurement asked whether we can convert escrow into credits if they expand into Dedicated later.

Emma — looping you here so we can clarify what's most important (predictability vs zero-upfront). Any signal on whether Carlisle would prefer a refundable deposit vs true escrow?

If we agree, I'll produce a short SOW and a single-sheet summary for procurement.

Thanks,
Mina Haddad

Subject: Re: HIPAA onboarding: HSM escrow vs metered KMS — decision and finance ask

Mina, short thoughts inline.

> Option A: Upfront HSM escrow (one-time onboarding fee amortized over 12 months) + discounted per-token inference pricing.
- Pros: predictable revenue and covers our provisioning risk. Cons: procurement pushback unless escrow converts to credit on upgrade.

> Option B: No upfront escrow, metered KMS (per-1k key ops) and higher recurring premium for HSM-backed operations.
- Pros: easier procurement acceptance. Cons: higher unit economics for us early; hit to margin if usage spikes.

> Option C: Hybrid — small onboarding deposit (refundable against 12-month commit) + blended metered KMS with step-down after commit thresholds.
- I like C as the default commercial compromise. Propose refundable deposit = 30% of one-month expected HSM infrastructure run rate, refundable as credits if they upgrade to Dedicated in 12 months.

Also: add an explicit clause in SOW that HSM onboarding is contingent on a 6-8 week schedule and that escrow funds only cover provisioning and a single certificate rotation. Any additional hardware or migrations bill separately.

If procurement wants straight Option B, ask for a 6-month minimum commitment at a slightly higher rate (we can table a step-down after 6 months).

Putting Stephanie on copy to vet the margin and credit mechanics.

—Ben
Ben Carter | Head, Strategic Sales Ops
ben_carter@redwood.com

Thanks Mina — and thanks Ben for the options.

Quick answers from Carlisle procurement side: predictability is higher priority than zero-upfront. They are open to a refundable deposit that converts to credits if we expand. They also want clear metering definitions (what counts as a key op, how we bill multi-region key access) and a cap on accidental overage in the first 90 days.

For timeline: can we have a one-page commercial summary + SOW draft by EOD next Thurs (Apr 5)? Legal will want HSM provisioning schedule and an onboarding checklist that we can attach to the PO.

Requests:
- Please include 90-day overage cap language.
- If escrow is refundable-as-credit on upgrade, specify credit expiry (we prefer 18 months).
- We will need a DocuSign-ready order form and a procurement contact for invoice sequencing.

Procurement team (procurement@carlislehealth.com) — flagging for follow-up on PO process.

Best,
